title: Calculated risk
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you take risks, or do you calculate them?
A student said the person in the book does not value money. He would sleep under an overpass to be in a space where he puts all his money on the line.
I said he realizes he needs money, but he doesn't let money be a distraction to the mission. He understands it is a consequence of the mission.

Let's pay attention to the evidence of how he mitigates risk, I said. It comes across as: I'll risk everything, like the poker game where he kept doubling until he won and then walked away with the money. But I think he is very calculated in his risk.
A student found the evidence: how he thinks about cost against the overall cost of everything. I read the passage from the book.
which calculated how much more costly a finished product was than the cost of the basic materials.

So he is mitigating risk, I said. He is not just going and buying a rocket that is overpriced. He asks what the components are, and what the carbon fibre, the metal and the fuel cost. I'm not going to believe anything at face value.
A student said another lesson: after his risk assessment and the cost of everything, he concluded they could do it themselves. They just needed the information, the data and the qualified people.
What is the real cost of the thing you buy or sell?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the price of something you buy often.
Write what its basic parts cost.
Write the gap between them, as a multiple.
Write the risk you take that is calculated and the risk that is only nerve.
Write what you could build yourself if you gathered the data and the people.
